prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses was $6.24 million and $18.98 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to a provision for credit losses of $12.10 million and $47.09 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025, respectively. On a linked-quarter basis, the provision for credit losses for the second quarter of 2026 was $4.96 million. The provision for credit losses for the first nine months of 2025 included provision expense of $18.73 million recorded for purchased non-PCD loans from Piedmont. United’s provision for credit losses relates to its portfolio of loans and leases, available-for-sale securities and held-to-maturity securities are discussed in more detail in the following paragraphs.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the provision for loan and lease losses was $6.24 million as compared to a provision for loan and lease losses of $12.10 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The lower amount of provision expense for the third quarter of 2026 was mainly due to higher provision for the commercial real estate nonowner-occupied (“CRE NOO”) loan segment for the third quarter of 2025. The provision for loan and lease losses for the first nine months of 2026 was $18.98 million as compared to a provision for loan and lease losses of $47.09 million for the first nine months of 2025.

nonint.text: Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 increased $9.97 million or 6.80% from the third quarter of 2025. For the first nine months of 2026, noninterest expense increased $15.91 million or 3.55% from the first nine months of 2025. Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 increased $2.00 million, or 1.29%, from the second quarter of 2026.

nonop.heading: Other Income
nonop.text:
Other income consists of all revenues, which are not included in interest and fee income related to earning assets. Noninterest income has been and will continue to be an important factor for improving United’s profitability. Recognizing the importance, management continues to evaluate areas where noninterest income can be enhanced.

Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $30.85 million, a decrease of $12.36 million or 28.61% from the third quarter of 2025. Noninterest income for the first nine months of 2026 was $103.41 million which was relatively flat from the first nine months of 2025, decreasing $804 thousand or less than 1%.

Fees from brokerage services for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 increased $342 thousand or 5.46% and $4.00 million or 23.86%, respectively, from the third quarter and first nine months of 2025 due to higher volume driven by growth in the business.

Net losses on investment securities were $348 thousand for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to net gains on investment securities of $10.44 million for the third quarter of 2025. The net losses on investment securities of $348 thousand for the third quarter of 2026 were due primarily to an unrealized fair value net loss on equity securities as compared to an unrealized fair value net gain on equity securities of $10.44 million for the third quarter of 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: For the third quarter of 2026, income tax expense was $33.44 million which was relatively flat from the third quarter of 2025, decreasing $298 thousand or less than 1%. This slight decrease in income tax expense was primarily due to lower earnings partially offset by a higher effective tax rate. For the first nine months of 2026, income tax expense was $97.99 million, an increase of $10.26 million or 11.70% from the first nine months of 2025. This increase in income tax expense was primarily due to higher earnings partially offset by a lower effective tax rate. On a linked-quarter basis, income tax expense increased $672 thousand or 2.05% from the second quarter of 2026. This increase in income tax expense was primarily due to a higher effective tax rate partially offset by lower earnings. United’s effective tax rate was 20.62% for the third quarter of 2026, 20.51% for the third quarter of 2025 and 19.96% for the second quarter of 2026. For the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, United’s effective tax rate was 20.32% and 20.72%, respectively.

net.text: Net income for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 was $128.70 million and $384.28 million, respectively, as compared to earnings of $130.75 million and $335.78 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2025. Diluted earnings per share were $0.94 for the third quarter of 2026 and $0.92 for the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share were $2.77 for the first nine months of 2026 as compared to $2.36 for the first nine months of 2025. On a linked-quarter basis, net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $131.38 million or $0.95 per diluted share.

ocf.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cash of $433.75 million was provided by operating activities due mainly to net income of $384.28 million. Net cash of $1.34 billion was used in investing activities which was primarily due to the aforementioned loan growth of $761.46 million and net purchases of investment securities of $569.38 million. During the first nine months of 2026, net cash of $246.71 million was provided by financing activities primarily due to growth in deposits of $649.81 million partially offset by the net acquisition of $235.03 million in treasury stock, cash dividends paid of $159.26 million and the net repayment of securities sold under agreements to repurchase of $13.76 million. The net effect of the cash flow activities was a decrease in cash and cash equivalents of $659.86 million for the first nine months of 2026.

wc.text: Other assets increased $28.44 million or 9.44% from year-end 2025 as deferred tax assets increased $22.60 million due mainly to a decrease in the fair value of available for sale securities, accounts receivable increased $6.80 million due to timing differences, income tax receivable increased $2.04 million, and OREO increased $2.34 million. Partially offsetting these increases was a decrease in core deposit intangibles of $5.51 million due to amortization.

capex.text: United anticipates it can meet its obligations over the next 12 months and has no material commitments for capital expenditures. United also has lines of credit available. See Notes 8 and 9 to the accompanying unaudited Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for more details regarding the amounts available to United under lines of credit.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: Net interest income represents the primary component of United’s earnings. It is the difference between interest income from earning assets and interest expense incurred to fund these assets. Net interest income is impacted by changes in the volume and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, as well as changes in market interest rates. Such changes, and their impact on net interest income in 2026 and 2025, are presented on the following page.

Noninterest income.text: For the third quarter of 2026, noninterest income decreased $12.36 million or 28.61% from the third quarter of 2025 while noninterest income for the first nine months of 2026 was relatively flat from the first nine months of 2025, decreasing $804 thousand or less than 1%. Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 decreased $7.66 million, or 19.90%, from the second quarter of 2026.

intro.text: United Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: UBSI) is a financial services company with consolidated assets of approximately $34 billion as of June 30, 2026. United is the 39 th largest banking company in the U.S. based on market capitalization. It is the parent company of United Bank, which comprises over 240 offices located across Washington, D.C., Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Georgia. For more information, visit ubsi-inc.com .
